title: Test suite performance: fewer git processes, deterministic contention, parallel packages
description:
The gate is 'go test -short -count=1 -timeout 45m -parallel 12 ./...' and it runs in FULL for every tick closed. Run epic-9pd ran it 49 times: roughly 20 minutes idle, 45-60+ under load, so the gate - not the work - dominated the epic's wall clock.

Profiling found the cost is not git, and not the tests' logic. It is process creation and one spinning loop.

Measured on this machine:
- ONE reconcile end-to-end test spawns 1148 git processes in 18 seconds (172 rev-parse, 109 fetch, 91 cat-file, 90 write-tree, 90 read-tree, 87 push, 75 update-index, 75 commit-tree, 46 hash-object).
- A git process costs 21.6ms to spawn; the same query through a long-lived 'git cat-file --batch' costs 0.90ms. 24x.
- internal/runstate spends 32s of its 50.7s in two tests that run an unthrottled 'for { git fetch }' goroutine, burning a core each.
- Four of five slow packages are effectively single-threaded: -parallel 12 does nothing without t.Parallel(). internal/exec/subprocess is 65.3s serial against a ~8s parallel wall.

What this epic must NOT do: replace git with a library. Every serious defect this project has found - FETCH_HEAD, the missing --refmap=, the shared peek ref, ref-lock contention, the ssh hang - lives in real git's behaviour, and a reimplementation would have let all of them through. The axis is fewer processes for the SAME git, using the streaming plumbing git already ships for exactly this.

Order matters: the load-sensitive tests (cy2) are fixed first, because raising parallelism makes contention worse, and a gate that refuses innocent work costs an hour per false refusal.
acceptance_criteria:
[A1] The full suite — go test -timeout 45m -parallel 12 ./..., what `make test` runs and CI's go job and epic close-out run — completes in under half its current wall clock on an idle machine, measured the same way (time the command on a quiet host, before and after). The per-tick gate is `go test -short` and has skipped the end-to-end tests since tick miu (2026-09-20), so it is not what this measures: the suite this epic profiles lives in the full run.
[A2] No test asserts on a condition it can sample rather than wait for.
[A3] Every defect class the current suite catches is still caught: the FETCH_HEAD, refmap, peek-ref and ref-lock regressions each still fail their guard when reintroduced.
[A4] Nothing in the run's durable-evidence semantics changes without its own tick saying so.
